page: Microsoft Azure HB176-96rs_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the HBv4 server family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

For local storage, the server includes a bundled 4332 GB NVMe SSD. It is also designated as Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external storage options. Additionally, the instance is RDMA capable, supporting low-latency, high-throughput networking interfaces, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

This server represents a high-density resource profile, balancing a large memory footprint with substantial local NVMe storage and high-core-count compute. The lack of integrated GPUs positions it away from hardware-accelerated deep learning, focusing instead on memory-intensive and high-performance computing workloads. It is suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive simulations, and enterprise workloads requiring RDMA networking and fast local scratch storage.
